subject: CONTRACT request (frontend -> kernel): reserve imported target surfaces at commit, so 'scheduled' can be reported at commit (kills ~12-19 ms of submit CPU on CA's path)
body:
GOAL
backboardd swaps right after commitAndWaitUntilSubmitted. Today we may only report 'scheduled' after the LAST SUBMIT_JM. The 0097(c) swap hold can only see surfaces that submitted jobs declare in write_mask. With a reservation taken at commit, the frontend reports scheduled immediately. Our executor then prepares and submits on its own thread while CA builds the next frame. The kernel holds the swap until the GPU finishes writing.

SELECTORS (new; same arg validation style as 0090; both on the 0111 trap path)
1) NORD2_GPU_SEL_SURFACE_RESERVE = 13
   - Input: scalarIn[0] = n (0..8). structIn = uint32_t handles[n]: this context's import handles (IMPORT_SURFACE replies) of the IOSurfaces the command will write.
   - Output: scalarOut[0] = reservation id R (nonzero, per-context monotonic). n=0 answers {R=0, kIOReturnSuccess}. That is the AVAILABILITY PROBE: it must succeed with R=0 on a kernel that has the selector. (Learn from WAIT_SEQ(0): define the probe answer explicitly.)
   - Errors:
     - kIOReturnBadArgument: n>8, unknown handle, or a handle that is not an imported surface.
     - kIOReturnBusy: more than 4 unretired reservations in this context. The frontend then falls back to scheduled-after-submit for that command.
   - Effect: from return until retired/cancelled, nord2_gpu_surface_busy(S) is true for each surface S behind those handles, for every client, with the same check the vsync handler uses today (swap goes back to the queue, at most 6 ticks / 100 ms, then busy_forced).
2) NORD2_GPU_SEL_SURFACE_RETIRE = 14
   - Input: scalarIn[0] = R, scalarIn[1] = seq.
   - seq != 0: R stays busy until every job of this context with id <= seq is terminal. Any terminal state releases: done, faulted or reset; a failed frame is still released, so the panel never deadlocks.
   - seq == 0: cancel immediately. The command failed before or while submitting.
   - Unknown R: kIOReturnNotFound. R == 0: success, no-op.
   - Must not block. Retire happens on the executor thread right after the command's last submit, or at chain_end.

LIFETIME / SAFETY
- Client close or context reset drops all of its reservations.
- An unretired reservation older than 200 ms stops counting as busy, and is counted in a new FB PRESENT field (resv_expired). This bounds any frontend bug to the existing busy_forced behaviour.
- Stats: add resv=<reserves>/<retires>/<cancels>/<expired> to the NORD2 GPU JOBS line.
- Ordering: RESERVE returns only after the reservation is visible to the vsync handler (take the same lock nord2_gpu_surface_busy takes).

FRONTEND SIDE (mine, after the kernel lands)
- At commit, on CA's thread: collect the imported surface targets the command writes. That is the colour/depth attachments with surfaceImported, at most 8; more means fall back.
- Call RESERVE, then report scheduled (status 3, scheduled handlers). Executor and early FIFO as today.
- RETIRE(R, completion seq) after the last submit; RETIRE(R, 0) on any error path.
- Without the selector (probe != {0, R=0}) or on Busy: today's early-at-submission path, unchanged.
- At most 2 frames in flight stays.

HOST MODEL
I will add both selectors to the bridge-test fake: reservations, retire by seq, cancel, Busy at the limit. Tests: the frame stays busy until its last job completes; cancel; probe; expiry.
